name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **bold, full-width focus ring** (4px, 2:1 contrast ratio) on all interactive elements.

This ensures keyboard users see clear focus at a glance, meeting WCAG 2.2’s 2:1 minimum contrast for focus indicators. The trade-off is slightly thicker rings may feel heavier in dense UIs, but clarity outweighs minimal visual bulk.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s bold ring risks a siren effect for keyboard users—it screams “error” or “alert” when it’s just navigation. A 4px ring also bleeds into dense layouts, crowding touch targets on mobile. Swap to a 2px ring with 3:1 contrast; test it with Playwright MCP’s keyboard nav suite and user feedback to settle the argument.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 2px solid ring with 3:1 contrast, inset 1px from the element. This keeps focus visible without the siren effect or layout crowding, meeting WCAG’s minimum contrast while preserving touch targets. The trade-off is slightly less immediate visibility for keyboard users in complex layouts, but that’s preferable to the false alerts and mobile clutter of a 4px ring.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-8308, worker-4518, worker-8014 — done, dissolved]

name: Reader
text: A 2px inset ring risks being missed on high-DPI or low-contrast screens—WCAG’s 3:1 minimum isn’t enough for users with visual impairments. Test a 3px ring with 4.5:1 contrast instead; settle the argument with Playwright MCP’s keyboard suite and user testing with screen-reader users who rely on focus visibility.
